notes:
POC summary & autoscaling/capacity notes:
- Core ask: predictable throughput for chat support + near-real-time reranking. Target SLOs: p95 <= 120ms for short-turn responses (~32 tokens), p99 <= 350ms; 99.95% uptime target.
- Traffic profile: diurnal spikes driven by support shifts. Baseline concurrent requests ~300-500, peak bursts up to ~2k reqs for short windows (5-20m).
- Current POC infra: 4x H100-equivalent GPUs reserved in staging. Observed during 24h test: sustained throughput ~650 req/s for 32-token gen with batching; p95=98ms, p99=260ms at current batch configs.
- Bottlenecks seen: cold-start time for model instances ~60-90s (cold VM + model load). KV-cache warm-up improves p95 by ~30% after initial warm period.
- Autoscaling policy under evaluation: scale-up trigger = queue length > 50 OR gpu_util > 75% for 30s; scale-up step = +2 GPUs (min step 1), max concurrent scale-up to not exceed budgeted reserve. Desired scale-up latency <= 60s.
- Scale-down policy: cool-down 15m after last scale-up; scale-down trigger = queue length < 10 AND gpu_util < 40% for 10m. Aim to avoid flapping during short bursts.
- Warm pool proposal: maintain a warm pool of 6 pre-loaded model workers (warm-cache primed) per region to reduce cold-starts; estimated standby GPU overhead ~15% of reserved capacity. Warm pool warm-up time ~10-20s vs cold 60-90s.
- Queueing: plan to apply bounded queue with backpressure at 2.5k requests; SLA-aware prioritization for premium routes. Suggested max queue length per route 200 requests; overflow behavior = drop or reroute to lower-cost model variant.
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: route to quantized 4-bit variant or smaller context model when reserved cluster saturated; fallback path adds ~30-60ms average latency but preserves throughput.
- Reserved GPU planning: recommended committed baseline = 8 GPUs for initial Dedicated contract (covers baseline + warm pool overhead) with burst capacity to 12 GPUs for predictable spikes. Discussing monthly committed hours vs flat monthly SKU pricing.
- SLA negotiation points to finalize: exact p95/p99 bands per route, credits for misses (sliding scale), maintenance windows (monthly 2h), and emergency scale guarantees for major incidents.
- Security/compliance: require VPC peering, SSO/SAML, KMS integration for keys, and audit log retention 1 year. On-prem validation: 2-week validation window requested by security.
- Quote from CTO on 2026-02-18 call: "We need inference to be as predictable as our DB cluster — if latency jumps under burst, product impact is immediate."
- Cost sensitivity: strong — procurement pushing for committed GPU discounts; wants clear cost for warm pool overhead and burst hours.
- Open questions: how Redwood accounts for warm pool standby cost in committed vs burst billing; can Redwood guarantee scale-up time SLAs or provide firm burst capacity? Also need detailed network egress pattern for compliance.
- Next steps: Redwood to provide: 1) recommended committed GPU SKU and pricing breakdown including warm pool; 2) draft SLA with p95/p99 bands + credits; 3) on-prem validation checklist and estimated time to validate. IronBridge to schedule architecture deep-dive week of 2026-03-15.
additional_context: IronBridge is a fast-growing CX SaaS vendor with strict latency SLAs for paying customers; they prefer a mix of reserved Dedicated capacity plus private deployment for EU data residency. Technical contacts are senior infra and SRE leads; legal procurement already engaged.
